# Option defaults

Every option of the original's two configuration sources, with what silvermere does with it.
`docs/config.md` is the reference for the keys that exist; this page records the range the
original enforced, both candidate defaults, and the options that do not survive. T-017 implements
`GameConfig` from it.

The original read its options from two places:

- **`WCCMMUD.MSG`** (71 option entries, of which 6 are text blocks): yes/no, numeric, character,
  token and string options. A numeric option is **clamped** to its range. The sysop edited the compiled
  file; the value shipped in the distribution is the one the running game used, because the game reads
  the file at start-up and it replaces the compiled-in defaults.
- **`WCCMMUD.INI`** (34 options): lines of `NAME=VALUE` and `#` comments, numbers read without
  range checks except `RACE_CHANGE_DURATION`. The distribution has **no** `WCCMMUD.INI`; every default is
  the one the game uses when the file is absent.

Regenerate this page with `python3 -I tools/msgconv/msgconv.py --msg WCCMMUD.MSG --options docs/config-defaults.md`
(the `.MSG` comes from the distribution `WCCMMUD_1.11p_DOS_MBBSEmu_v2.zip`).

## Conventions

- **Module default**: the compiled-in value, the one the game has before the option file is read.
- **Shipped value**: the value in the distributed `WCCMMUD.MSG` (the game as the captures saw it).
- **GameConfig default**: what `silvermere-types::config::GameConfig::default()` has. For `.MSG` options it is
  the shipped value (John, 2026-10-14), except `inactive_secs = 3600`; for INI options the module default.
  `characters_per_account = 1` and `open_signup = true` are also John's. The test `crates/silvermere-text/tests/msg_catalogue.rs`
  checks this column against `GameConfig::default()`.
- **TOML key**: `[game]` in `silvermere.toml`, the snake_case of the original name unless noted.

### Defaults

John decided on 2026-10-14 that the `.MSG` options default to the **shipped** value, so the GameConfig
default equals the shipped value for every row above, except `INACTIVE` (`inactive_secs = 3600`; the file
ships `900`) and `INVGLO1`..`INVGLO10` (one list, `inv_glo`). The module default is kept in the table for
the record. Note that `pun_hup = "none"` makes `min_hup_hp`, `max_hup_hp` and `max_hup_items` moot until
a sysop turns hang-up punishment on.

## `WCCMMUD.MSG` keys that become roles

`SYSOPKEY` and `GAMOPKEY` are BBS key names a user needed to run sysop and game-op commands. silvermere has
roles instead; T-013 maps `SYSOPKEY` to the `sysop` role and `GAMOPKEY` to
`gameop`. `GOSSKEY` and `AUCTKEY` were keys that *remove* a channel from a user; T-013 maps them to per-account
mute flags. The names of the keys are not configuration any more.

| Option | Type | Range | Shipped value | Defined at | Role mapping |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `SYSOPKEY` | string | up to 15 characters | `wccsysop` | WCCMMUD.MSG:46 | Role name `sysop` (T-013). Shipped key `wccsysop`. |
| `GAMOPKEY` | string | up to 15 characters | `wccgameop` | WCCMMUD.MSG:52 | Role name `gameop` (T-013). Shipped key `wccgameop`. |
| `GOSSKEY` | string | up to 15 characters | `gidiot` | WCCMMUD.MSG:102 | Role name `gossip-ban` (a key that removes gossip; T-013 maps it to a muted-channel flag). |
| `AUCTKEY` | string | up to 15 characters | `aidiot` | WCCMMUD.MSG:108 | Role name `auction-ban` (a key that removes auction; T-013 maps it to a muted-channel flag). |

the game.

In silvermere accounts own their characters, so deleting an account deletes them (the original's `YES`). The `NO` mode lets a new account that reuses the name inherit the old character, which is a BBS-ism with no use here. |

The text blocks of `WCCMMUD.MSG` (`USRLOGIN`, `USRLOGOF`, `USRFOLED`, `USREXIT`, `LEAVEMNU`, `INACHUP`) are
in `crates/silvermere-text/messages/wccmmud.toml`; `USRLOGOF` (disabled in the original) and `LEAVEMNU` (a
sub-board hook) are kept there as unused entries. The text blocks of `WCCTEXT.MSG` are in `wcctext.toml`,
without the two full-screen-display templates `EDITCHA1` and `EDTCHAN2`, which are kept as assets for
character creation (T-063) in `crates/silvermere-text/messages/assets/`. The help topics of `WCCMMHLP.MSG`
are in `help_topics.toml`.

## Differences from the original

- **Reject, not clamp.** The numeric `.MSG` options and `RACE_CHANGE_DURATION` replaced an out-of-range value
  with the nearest limit and carried on. `GameConfig::validate` stops start-up with exit code 1 and names the
  key and the range, for every ranged key. The reason is the same as for the rest of the configuration: a typo
  such as `inactive_secs = 3` should be a message, not a silent 60. The ranges themselves are unchanged.
- **`pun_hup`.** The original treated any word other than the four as `HIGH`. silvermere rejects any other
  word.
- **Tournament play** (`tournament_play = true`) forces `enable_lawful` to false and `lvl_diff` to 100 at load;
  the engine applies this, the values in the file are left alone.
- **`sec_oth`** is rounded down to whole minutes with a minimum of 60 seconds before use;
  the engine applies this.
- **`DEATHHP`** has a check for a value above 2000 that the range makes impossible; it is not carried.

## Decisions on the options the first configuration card left out

- **`PROFCHEK` survives** as `game.profanity_check`, default `false` (module default 0, shipped `NO`). It is an
  optional filter on `say`, `yell` and the gossip-class lines; the card that implements those commands brings
  the word list.
- **`EXPINTEN` survives** as `game.exp_in_topten`, default `true`. It shows experience in the TOPTEN list.
- **`DELUSER` is dropped.** Accounts own their characters; deleting an account deletes them. The `NO` setting
  (a new account that reuses a deleted account's name inherits the character) exists only because the BBS user
  file and the game's character file were separate.
- **`CODEC_OF_TWINKS` is kept** as an integer (`game.codec_of_twinks`, default 0) with its note: it is a developer
  code that unlocks sysop debug tools when it equals 78.

`GameConfig` has `profanity_check`, `exp_in_topten`, `codec_of_twinks` and `sys_log_deaths`. The two bools
`sys_reset_rooms` and `sys_disable_gangs` it had before are removed: the originals were BBS key names, so they
are roles like the other 17 `SYS_*_KEY` options (T-013), not game settings.

## silvermere additions

- **`game.cleanup.tz`** (silvermere addition, not in the original): the IANA time zone `game.cleanup.at` is read
  in. Default `America/Detroit` (source: John, 2026-10-15). It is checked at config load with
  `jiff::tz::TimeZone::get`; an unknown name is a config error naming `game.cleanup.tz`. The Docker image runs in
  UTC, so without it the cleanup would run at the wrong hour.
